scenes.name: the two numbers, counted from the shapes
scenes.visual: Dark canvas, one continuous two-row ledger: prefill in the top half, decode in the bottom half, identical layout and one shared scale, so the rows compare directly. Frame 1920 x 1080; keep x < 420, y < 110 free for the chapter label. Left column, x 60 to 420, the inputs. Prefill: 2,000 blue token pills in a 40 x 50 grid, each pill 7 x 4 px at a 9 px column pitch and 6 px row pitch, so the grid spans x 60 to 420, y 190 to 490, with a grey tag '2,000 tokens' centred under it at y 515. Decode: one blue pill, 40 x 22 px, centred at (240, 740). Column x 450 to 520: a small stack of five blue weight tiles (60 x 36 px, each offset 3 px) beside each row's input, centred at (485, 340) and (485, 740); it stands for the weights in the memory beside the chip, and coral byte particles leave it along the bytes lane. Lanes: every bar starts at x = 600 and the full scale is 1,000 px (x 600 to 1600): 1,000 px is 290 trillion operations on an amber lane and 146 GB on a coral lane. Prefill row: heading at (60, 160); one-line equation at (600, 205); lane label 'operations' at (600, 248), amber bar y 265 to 295; lane label 'bytes moved' at (600, 343), coral bar y 360 to 390; grey sub-label right-aligned to x 1600 at y 418; result pill left-aligned at x 600, centred on y 465, 44 px tall. Decode row: the same layout exactly 400 px lower (heading y 560, operations bar y 665 to 695, bytes bar y 760 to 790, sub-label y 818, result pill y 865). A fraction slot for each row sits at x 1000 to 1450 beside its result pill. End tags are left-aligned at x 1615, at each bar's mid-height, and end before x 1880. Bottom band, centred at y 1000: one white summary line. Bar lengths, to scale: prefill 280 trillion is 966 px plus a lighter amber attention segment of 34 px, tagged schematic because its true share is 2 to 4 percent depending on how it is counted; prefill bytes are 959 px for 140 GB plus one hatched 41 px coral block for the extra 6 GB, drawn as a single schematic block, not split; decode's 140 billion operations are 0.48 px, a hairline shown through a magnifier; decode's 140 GB is 959 px, ending exactly under the prefill weights segment. Colour: operations amber, bytes coral, tokens and weights blue, text white and grey. Labels dim to 40% once they stop being the subject. The idea: two ratios counted from shapes, not measured; nearly identical bytes buy work that differs two-thousand-fold.

beats.say: Prefill first: a two-thousand-token prompt. Every token meets every weight once: two thousand times a hundred and forty billion operations, about two hundred and ninety trillion with attention.
beats.show: On 'Prefill first', the heading 'Prefill · 70B model · 2,000-token prompt' writes on at (60, 160). On 'two-thousand-token prompt', the 40 x 50 grid fills row by row in about one second and its tag '2,000 tokens' appears. On 'meets every weight once', one pill lifts out and passes through the weight stack, each tile flashing amber, while the amber equation writes on at (600, 205): '2 × 70 billion = 140 billion ops per token'. On 'two thousand times', the whole grid pulses, a wave sweeps through the stack, the equation morphs in place into '140 billion × 2,000 = 280 trillion' (one line, never two), and the amber bar sweeps from x 600 to 966 px with end tag '280 trillion'. On 'with attention', the lighter 34 px segment clicks onto the end, a small grey tag right-aligned under it reads 'attention: a few %, schematic', and the end tag morphs to 'about 290 trillion'.

beats.say: Yet the weights cross the bus once, a hundred and forty gigabytes, plus about six for activations and the running record. About two thousand operations per byte.
beats.show: The equation and the attention tag dim to 40%. On 'cross the bus once', a single dense stream of coral particles runs out of the weight stack along the bytes lane, once, and the coral bar grows to 959 px, end tag '140 GB'. On 'about six', the hatched 41 px block clicks onto the end, the tag becomes 'about 146 GB', and the grey sub-label writes on under the bar: 'weights, plus activations and cache writes'. On 'two thousand operations per byte', the two end tags fly into the fraction slot and stack, amber 'about 290 trillion' over coral 'about 146 billion', then collapse leftward into the result pill: '= about 2,000 ops per byte', outlined amber.

beats.say: Decode, one token for a lone request: a hundred and forty billion operations on the same hundred and forty gigabytes, every time, since the chip holds about a tenth of a gigabyte.
beats.show: The prefill grid, stack, lane labels and sub-label dim to 40%; its bars, end tags and result pill stay bright. On 'Decode', the heading 'Decode · one token · batch size one' writes on at (60, 560). On 'a lone request', one blue pill drops in at (240, 740). On 'a hundred and forty billion operations', the decode amber bar grows to its true 0.48 px, effectively invisible; a magnifier circle swoops onto x 600 and shows the hairline, with end tag 'about 140 billion' at (640, 680) and, under it in grey, 'drawn to scale: 1/2,000 of the bar above'. On 'the same hundred and forty gigabytes', a coral stream runs from the decode stack and the coral bar sweeps to 959 px, end tag '140 GB'; a thin white vertical guide joins its end to the end of the prefill weights segment directly above. On 'every time', the stream fires twice more, the bar flashing on each pass, and the sub-label 'the same weights, every time' writes on. On 'a tenth of a gigabyte', a small chip-outline icon pops up beside the decode stack with the grey tag 'chip holds ≈ 0.1 GB'; it fades at the end of the beat.

beats.say: Same model, same chip, both from the shapes alone: two thousand against one. Decode gets one operation from each identical byte.
beats.show: The magnifier, all lane labels, sub-labels and the drawn-to-scale tag fade, so only the two headings, the bars with their end tags and the result pills remain. On 'from the shapes alone', the decode fraction builds in its slot: amber '2 × 70 billion' over coral '70 billion × 2 bytes'; the two 2s strike through each other, then the two 70 billions, and it collapses into the decode result pill: '= about 1 op per byte', outlined coral. On 'two thousand against one', both result pills pulse together and the white summary line writes on at y 1000: 'Same model, same chip: 2,000 against 1'. On 'each identical byte', the white guide between the two 959 px coral segments pulses, and the decode bytes bar fills with a fine row of coral byte-blocks, each topped by one amber dot.

scenes.name: both phases on the roofline
scenes.visual: The H100 roofline exactly as ch11 left it, same coordinates as ch11_s05 to s07, so nothing changes shape between chapters. Horizontal axis 'operations per byte (log)', ticks 1, 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 at x = 320, 570, 820, 1070, 1320 (250 px per factor of ten); vertical axis 'trillion operations per second (log)', ticks 1, 10, 100, 1,000 at y = 900, 650, 400, 150 (also 250 px per factor of ten, so the slanted ceiling runs at exactly 45 degrees). The vertical axis line stands at x = 260, 60 px left of the intensity-1 tick (the axis starts at about 0.58), so a dot at intensity 1 sits clear of it; y tick labels are right-aligned to x 245. Plot clipped at y = 110. Amber flat ceiling at y = 151 (989 trillion) from the ridge to x 1320, tag '989 trillion/s' right-aligned above its right end at y 130. Coral slanted ceiling through (320, 769) and (570, 519) up to the ridge at (938, 151). White ridge marker at (938, 151) with a dashed vertical to the axis and the label 'ridge, 295' on the tick-label row at (938, 935), between the '100' and '1,000' ticks. Region tints at 10%: coral left of the ridge, amber right. Corner tag 'H100' at (340, 140). Workload dots: decode, coral, at (320, 769), label 'decode, intensity 1' to its lower right at (345, 795); prefill, amber, at (1145, 151), label 'prefill, intensity 2,000' just below it at (1145, 185). Sidebar x 1400 to 1880, ch11's formula column: two horizontal gauges 440 px long, 'arithmetic busy' in amber at y 330 and 'bus busy' in coral at y 440, each with a readout at its right end; from b3, the 30 ms thesis bar from ch05, redrawn 440 px wide at y 620. Brackets that measure distance run along y 870, just above the horizontal axis, except the prefill-to-ridge bracket, which runs above the flat ceiling at y 128. The idea: two dots two thousand times apart on one axis, and where each sits says by itself which resource is idle.

beats.say: On the roofline, prefill sits about seven times right of the ridge: arithmetic flat out, bandwidth to spare.
beats.show: The chart is already on screen as ch11 left it. On 'prefill', the amber dot drops onto the flat ceiling at (1145, 151) with its label. On 'seven times', a white bracket at y 128 spans x 938 to 1145, tag '× 7'. On 'arithmetic flat out', the 'arithmetic busy' gauge fills amber to '100%'; on 'bandwidth to spare', the 'bus busy' gauge fills coral to '≈ 15%' and stops, the rest of it hatched grey.

beats.say: Decode sits nearly three hundred times left, low on the slanted ceiling: bus almost always busy, arithmetic under one percent.
beats.show: The '× 7' bracket fades. On 'Decode', the coral dot drops onto the slanted ceiling at (320, 769) with its label; a 60 px white dotted line runs left from it to the axis at x 260, where a coral read-out tag sits on the axis at the dot's height: '3.35 trillion/s'. On 'nearly three hundred times', a white bracket along y 870 spans x 320 to 938, tag '× 295'. On 'bus almost always busy', the gauges switch to decode: 'bus busy' fills coral to '≈ 100%'; on 'under one percent', 'arithmetic busy' drains to an amber sliver, readout '0.34%'.

beats.say: That is where the thirty milliseconds went, and nothing is broken. The workload's shape leaves the chip able only to wait.
beats.show: The gauges and the '× 295' bracket fade. In the sidebar at y 620, the thesis bar from ch05 returns, 440 px wide: a 2 px amber sliver tagged 'arithmetic, under 1%' and the rest coral, with a small stopwatch icon reading '30 ms' above its left end. On 'thirty milliseconds went', a white label writes on over the coral part: 'waiting for weights'. On 'able only to wait', a small hourglass icon settles on the decode dot and the coral tint around it deepens from 10% to 25%.

beats.say: Two points, two thousand times apart. Almost everything ahead in this series tries to move the left one rightward.
beats.show: The thesis bar and the hourglass fade; only the axes, the two ceilings, the ridge and the two labelled dots remain. On 'two thousand times apart', a white bracket along y 870 spans x 320 to 1145, tag '× 2,000'. On 'move the left one rightward', a teal arrow grows out of the decode dot up along the slanted ceiling toward the ridge, and holds.

scenes.name: the hard throughput ceiling
scenes.visual: A new composition: decode's position turned into a speed limit. Centre-right, the GPU package illustration: an amber compute die, 260 x 260 px, centred at (1250, 560); two coral-outlined HBM stacks, 90 x 220 px, centred at (960, 560) and (1540, 560); between each stack and the die a wide bus channel along which coral particles flow at one steady speed. A thin ring of radius 175 around the die fills coral as particles arrive; each full ring stands for one complete 140 GB crossing, after which a blue token pill pops out of the die, arcs left into an output tray at x 140 to 620, y 520 to 600, and the ring resets. Cadence is slowed for readability: one ring every 1.2 s, about 29 times slower than the real 41.8 ms, with a small grey tag 'slowed down' beside the ring; the counter 'tokens per second' under the tray at (380, 680) always shows the true rate. Top band, centred at y 200: an equation that builds term by term and carries into the next scene. Top-right callout slot x 1480 to 1880, y 270 to 360. Bottom band, y 930: three grey condition chips. Colour: bytes and bandwidth coral, the token rate blue, the die amber. The idea: the token rate is a flow divided by a fixed load, and nothing inside the die can change it.

beats.say: On the bandwidth ceiling, bytes set decode's pace. Maximum tokens a second is bandwidth over bytes per token: the thirty-millisecond division, upside down. On an H one hundred, still our what-if, about twenty-four.
beats.show: The package draws on, coral particles start along both channels and the ring begins to fill. On 'bytes set decode's pace', the bus channels brighten while the die stays a dim amber. On 'Maximum tokens a second', the equation builds at y 200: blue 'max tokens per second', white '=', coral 'bandwidth', white '÷', coral 'bytes per token', each term landing on its word. On 'thirty-millisecond division', the callout appears in the top-right slot: a stopwatch icon with '≈ 30 ms' and the line 'H200: 140 GB ÷ 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms'; on 'upside down', its fraction flips in place to 'H200: 4.8 TB/s ÷ 140 GB = 34 tokens/s'. On 'H one hundred', 'bandwidth' morphs into '3.35 TB/s' and 'bytes per token' into '140 GB per token', and a grey tag under the equation's left end reads 'H100: a what-if, needs 2 chips'. On 'twenty-four', the result writes on in a white-outlined box at the equation's right, '≈ 24 tokens/s'; blue pills start popping into the tray, one per ring, and the counter runs to '23.9' and holds.

beats.say: A physical ceiling, not a software one: no cleverer kernel beats it, since even instant arithmetic waits for bytes.
beats.show: The callout and the what-if tag fade. On 'no cleverer kernel', the die flashes amber, a grey tag beside it reads 'faster kernel', and an amber readout on the die counts 'arithmetic: 0.14 ms' down to '0 ms'. On 'waits for bytes', the particles keep exactly their speed, the ring fills at the same pace, the next pill emerges only when it completes, and the counter stays at '23.9' with a grey 'no change' beside it.

beats.say: It bounds every serving system on this hardware: the most one answer can stream, and, at one token per read, the most the chip can make.
beats.show: The kernel tags fade. On 'every serving system', the bus channels glow coral and gain the label 'the limit: how fast the bus delivers weights', and a horizontal ceiling line tagged '24 tokens/s max' locks across the top of the tray. On 'this hardware', two grey condition chips appear in the bottom band, 'this chip' and '16-bit weights', joined by thin lines up to '3.35 TB/s' and '140 GB per token'. On 'one token per read', the third chip, 'one token per read', appears, joined to 'per token'.

scenes.name: the only three ways past it
scenes.visual: Continues straight on from the ceiling. The equation '≈ 24 tokens/s = 3.35 TB/s ÷ 140 GB per token' slides up to y 150 and stays; the three grey condition chips rise from the bottom band to sit beneath their terms at y 215. The package, tray and counter fade out. Header 'The only three ways past it' at y 290. Three teal cards, 520 x 440 px, at x 120 to 640, 700 to 1220 and 1280 to 1800, y 340 to 780: 'Raise bandwidth' over 'a different chip'; 'Shrink bytes per token' over 'lower precision, compression'; 'Amortise the transfer' over 'batching, or several at once'. Each card joins with a thin teal line to the condition chip and term it changes. Each card's lower 280 px holds a small worked example. Card 1: three horizontal bars to scale at 7 px per token per second, grey 'H100 · 3.35 TB/s' 168 px '24/s', teal 'H200 · 4.8 TB/s' 240 px '34/s', teal 'B200 · 8 TB/s' 400 px '57/s'. Card 2: a coral stack to scale, 200 px for 140 GB, halving to 100 px '70 GB' and 50 px '35 GB', with readouts '8-bit: ≈ 48/s' and '4-bit: ≈ 96/s'. Card 3: one coral read arrow fanning out to ten blue pills in slightly different shades, the line '140 GB ÷ 10 = 14 GB per token', a bracket '≈ 240 tokens/s' with a grey 'weights only' tag, and a separate pill that splits into three. As each card fills, the previous card's worked example dims to 40%, so at most one example is bright. Bottom band, y 860 to 1000: a teal path and one closing white line. The idea: the three ways out are exactly the three conditions under the equation, so the roadmap falls out of one line.

beats.say: There are only three ways past it, one per term. Raise bandwidth, with a different chip. Or shrink the bytes: eight-bit weights give about forty-eight tokens a second.
beats.show: On 'only three ways', the header writes on and three card outlines draw. On 'one per term', a teal line draws from each card up to its chip and term: card 1 to 'this chip' and '3.35 TB/s', card 2 to '16-bit weights' and '140 GB per token', card 3 to 'one token per read' and 'per token'. On 'Raise bandwidth', card 1 fills with its title and sub, and its bars grow in turn: the grey H100 reference, then H200 and B200 in teal, readouts '24/s', '34/s', '57/s'. On 'shrink the bytes', card 1's example dims and card 2 fills; on 'eight-bit', the 200 px coral stack '140 GB' halves to '70 GB', readout '8-bit: ≈ 48/s'; at the end of the beat it halves again to '35 GB', readout '4-bit: ≈ 96/s'.

beats.say: Or amortise each read: ten batched requests make about two hundred and forty a second, counting only the weights, each still at twenty-four. Or one answer takes several tokens per read.
beats.show: Card 2's example dims and card 3 fills. On 'ten batched requests', one coral read arrow fans out to ten blue pills in slightly different shades, one per request, and the line '140 GB ÷ 10 = 14 GB per token' writes on. On 'two hundred and forty', a bracket round all ten reads '≈ 240 tokens/s'; on 'counting only the weights', the small grey tag 'weights only' attaches to it. On 'each still at twenty-four', every pill gets a tiny '24/s'. On 'several tokens per read', a separate blue pill at the card's right edge splits into three pills of one answer, all fed by a single coral arrow, tag 'several at once · later'.

beats.say: Each becomes a later video. One line of arithmetic, and its three escape routes are the entire roadmap.
beats.show: All three worked examples fade, leaving the card titles and subs. On 'a later video', a small film-strip icon drops onto each card in turn. On 'One line of arithmetic', the equation at the top glows once. On 'the entire roadmap', a teal path draws beneath the three cards from left to right, and a white line writes on under it at y 960: 'three escape routes: the entire roadmap'.

checks.claim: Operations per token = 2 × 70 billion = 140 billion (decode, and each prefill token)
Prefill weight operations for a 2,000-token prompt = 2 × 70e9 × 2,000 = 280 trillion
Attention cost per query-key pair across the model (QK and softmax×V, 2 ops per multiply-add, 128 head dim, 64 heads, 80 layers) = 2,621,440 ops; reproduces fig 115's 5.4 GFLOP at 2,048 context

Attention inside a 2,000-token prefill adds 5.2 trillion (causal, 1.9%) to 10.5 trillion (full square, 3.7%): said as 'with attention' and tagged 'a few %, schematic' on screen, since the drawn 34 px segment cannot state which count applies
280 trillion plus attention = 285 to 290.5 trillion, so the atlas's 'about 290 trillion' is consistent
Extra prefill bytes beyond the weights: 146 - 140 = about 6 GB

Reconstruction (not stated in the atlas, and dependent on fusion assumptions) of the ~6 GB: residual activations read+written per layer 2,000 × 8,192 × 2 B × 2 × 80 = 5.24 GB, cache writes 2,000 × 327,680 B = 0.66 GB, total with weights 145.9 GB. Because it is a reconstruction, the film draws the 6 GB as one schematic block labelled 'activations and cache writes', not as a measured split
Prefill intensity: 290 trillion / 146 billion = 1,986, 'about 2,000'; without the extras 280 trillion / 140 billion = exactly 2,000
Decode intensity: (2 × 70e9 ops) / (70e9 × 2 bytes) = 1 op per byte; the 2s and the 70 billions cancel

CORRECTION (reviewer blocker): the chip holds 'about a tenth of a gigabyte' (132 SMs × 512 KB + 50 MB L2 ≈ 0.12 GB), not 'a few hundred kilobytes' for the whole chip; matches ch02 s02 b6 and ch09. 140 GB is ≈ 1,150 times that
Prefill about seven times right of the ridge (2,000 / 295 = 6.8); decode nearly 300 times left (295 / 1); the two dots 2,000 / 1 = 2,000 apart
Decode attainable = 1 op/byte × 3.35 TB/s = 3.35 trillion ops/s = 0.34% of the 989 trillion peak ('under one percent')
Same sliver as the 30 ms thesis bar from ch05: 0.1 / 30 = 0.33%
Prefill at peak: arithmetic 290e12 / 989e12 = 0.29 s; reading 146 GB / 3.35 TB/s = 43.6 ms; bus busy 14.9%, gauge '≈ 15%'
Decode on H100: arithmetic 140e9 / 989e12 = 0.14 ms; reading 140 GB / 3.35 TB/s = 41.8 ms
Decode on H200: 140 GB / 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms, the 'thirty milliseconds' (the one callout of it in this chapter, s03 b1)
Hard ceiling on H100: 3.35 TB/s / 140 GB = 23.9, 'about 24 tokens per second'
H100 is a what-if for this model: 140 GB needs 2 of its 80 GB chips
Raise bandwidth: H200 4.8 TB/s / 140 GB = 34 tokens/s; B200 8 TB/s / 140 GB = 57 tokens/s
Shrink bytes: 8-bit weights 70 GB give 47.9 tokens/s; 4-bit 35 GB give 95.7 tokens/s on 3.35 TB/s
Amortise: ten requests share one read, 140 GB / 10 = 14 GB per token, 3.35 TB/s / 14 GB = 239 tokens/s in total, shown and said as 'about 240'; each user still 23.9/s (weights only)

s01 bars at 1,000 px full scale (290 trillion ops, 146 GB): 280 T = 966 px, attention 34 px, 140 GB = 959 px, 6 GB = 41 px, decode's 140 billion ops = 0.48 px; ops ratio 290e12 / 140e9 = 2,071, tagged '1/2,000 of the bar above'
s02 roofline in ch11's coordinates (x = 320 + 250·log10(intensity), y = 900 - 250·log10(ops/s / 1e12)): decode (320, 769), ridge (938, 151), prefill (1145, 151)
